items.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
items.summary:
For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich

When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow.

More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can…
items.t: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing

items.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
items.summary:
Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad

This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.

Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16. “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.”

items.title: Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund
items.summary:
Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club

Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his highly anticipated debut. But after a week when Arsenal published an article dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager.

Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match.

items.title: Lights go out on Commanders before they beat Bengals in final seconds
items.summary:
• Cincinnati Bengals 20-22 Washington Commanders

  • Drew Stevens kicks game-winning field goal

  • Game delayed after lights go out in third quarter

Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired, and the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night.

After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal, Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati eight-yard line. Daniels spiked the ball again with five seconds left and Stevens did the rest.

items.t: Lights go out on Commanders before they beat Bengals in final seconds

Smith was hardly an outlier. Other pundits, as well as some Manchester United fans, also questioned Bryan Mbeumo’s focus and professionalism after he posted an image of GTA VI and the word “historique” after midnight on Thursday. Meanwhile before last weekend’s Premier League games, the Odd Sport social media account predicted that Chelsea, Brighton and Manchester City would all lose. Why? Because their younger squads might be more focused on Vice City than their opponents, and therefore play with less intensity as a result. Max Verstappen has said his outstanding victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday was not really true to the spirit of Formula One and how he wants to race.

Verstappen took a remarkable win, defending his lead and retaking it time and time again after it changed hands 35 times in a race dominated by the cars slipstreaming each other.

items.title: ‘Ollie makes it sound easy’: Crocombe on fast-track with Test debut in his sights
items.summary:
England seamer, who now has Jimmy Anderson as a county teammate, hopes a red-ball bow is not too far away

Henry Crocombe is a cricketer in a hurry. Thoughts of playing for England were far from the fast bowler’s mind at the start of 2026, but he has since appeared in all three squads, made his debut in two formats and swapped Sussex for Surrey.

The winter move to the Oval has come in part due to the financial problems at Hove. But the chance to play and train at a Test ground made it a no-brainer when Alec Stewart sat him down at the Fentiman Arms in SW8 with a contract offer. The subsequent signing of Jimmy Anderson was simply an added bonus.
